results.title: CARMA 2026 | July 1 – 3, 2026 · Valencia, Spain. Internet and Big Data in Economics and Social Sciences
results.content: ## July 1 – 3, 2026 · Valencia, Spain. Internet and Big Data in Economics and Social Sciences. #### ***AI, Internet Data and Computational Methods in Social Sciences***. **8th International Conference on Advanced Research Methods and Analytics**. 1 – 3 July, 2026 · Valencia, Spain. Research methods in economics and social sciences are evolving rapidly with the rise of **AI-driven analytics**, **Large Language Models (LLMs)**, and **causal machine learning**. The increasing availability of Internet and Big Data sources has enabled new forms of measurement, inference, and theory testing. As these sources, methods, and applications become more interdisciplinary, the **8th International Conference on Advanced Research Methods and Analytics (CARMA 2026)** provides a consolidated forum for researchers and practitioners to exchange ideas and advances on how emerging computational and data-intensive methods are applied to social and economic phenomena, and to discuss the opportunities and challenges they bring. Topics of interest include, but are not limited to, the following areas:. * **Internet and Big Data sources**. + Google Trends and Search Engine data. + Web scraping and online content analysis. + Geospatial, sensor, and mobile phone data. + Multimodal and heterogeneous data integration. + Synthetic data generation for research. * **Data Science and Machine Learning Methods in social sciences**. + AI and machine learning applications. + Causal inference with observational data. + Large Language Models (LLMs) and generative AI applications. + Sentiment, topic, and narrative analysis. + Data validation, quality and reproducibility. * **Applications in Economics and Social Sciences**. + eWOM and social media marketing. + Business analytics and digital marketing. + Data-driven innovation and competitiveness. + Data economy, governance and regulation. + Digital platforms and market structures. + e-Government and data-driven policy. + Economic inequality in the data economy. The Scientific Committee is particularly interested in receiving submissions that showcase applied and empirical research of significant interest to scholars of the social sciences. The CARMA 2026 conference will be held on 1 – 3 July 2026 at the Faculty of Business Administration and Management of the Universitat Politècnica de València (UPV), which has been recently ranked as the best technical university in Spain by the *Academic Ranking of World Universities* (ARWU) 2025.

results.title: Causal Inference Research and Practice: Latest Trends and Developments
results.content: Machine learning and causal inference. Bayesian methods and causal inference. It is a key skill for analytical reasoning, as it helps you understand the causal mechanisms behind complex phenomena, evaluate policies and programs, and make informed decisions. In this article, we will explore some of the latest developments and trends in causal inference research and practice, and how they can enhance your analytical reasoning abilities. Some of the latest developments and trends in causal inference research and practice include the integration of machine learning techniques with causal inference methods, the exploration of causal discovery algorithms for high-dimensional data, and the growing focus on causal inference in areas like healthcare, economics, and policy evaluation. ## 3 Machine learning and causal inference. Causal inference can benefit from machine learning techniques, such as propensity score matching, regression discontinuity, instrumental variables, and mediation analysis, to estimate causal effects from large and complex datasets. Machine learning can also benefit from causal inference principles, such as causal structure learning, causal discovery, and causal inference testing, to improve the interpretability and robustness of machine learning models. Machine learning employs various algorithms for recognizing patterns and also making forecasts while causal inference tries to study cause-effect relationships for instance through propensity score matching or regression discontinuity to calculate causal effects even from complicated data sets; both sets of knowledge can be integrated by these techniques. ## 4 Bayesian methods and causal inference. Bayesian methods can also use causal inference concepts, such as causal graphs, causal models, and causal effects, to enhance the validity and reliability of Bayesian analysis. In causal inferences, Bayesian exponents such as causal networks and inference assist in investigating cause-effect relationships, fusing data together or making choices in the face of adversity. On the other hand, causal inference models like effect sizes and diagrams increase both the accuracy and reliability of Bayesian analyses when it comes to understanding why things happen. Causal inference goes beyond mere correlation to reveal genuine cause-and-effect relationships thus facilitating wise choices in sectors like marketing, business and public policy among others. If you want to learn more about causal inference and improve your analytical reasoning skills, there are many resources available online and offline.

results.title: Sage Research Methods - Mixed Methods for Policy Research and Program Evaluation - Designing and Implementing Fully Integrated Mixed Methods Research
results.content: This practical text equips students, researchers, and policymakers in the social sciences with the tools they need for applying mixed methods in policy research and program evaluation, from design, through data collection, and dissemination. Emphasizing the “how-to”—the set of conceptual and active tasks carried out by mixed methods researchers—the book is illustrated with rich case studies from the authors’ own research projects in education and public policy. These examples help readers identify and explain policy and program impacts and better understand the “why” and “how” of observed effects. Throughout the book, the authors describe challenges that both beginners and advanced scholars are likely to encounter when doing mixed methods research and recommend practical tools available to address them. icon backBack to table of contents. # Designing and Implementing Fully Integrated Mixed Methods Research. * **In:**Mixed Methods for Policy Research and Program Evaluation. * **Subject:**Political Science and International Relations, Social Policy and Public Policy, Sociology. * Show page numbers Hide page numbers. ### Designing and Implementing Fully Integrated Mixed Methods Research. ### Introduction. Policy and evaluation research are often undertaken collaboratively, with the individual researcher or research team engaging policy designers, program implementers, the target population, and other program stakeholders to understand an intervention’s implementation and impacts and what drives them. In this regard, the benefits of striving toward a fully integrated mixed methods approach—in empirically investigating patterns across units to identify associations and plausible causal relationships and simultaneously digging deeper to explore the potential causal pathways and policy and contextual factors that intervene in them—seem so obvious that one might expect this approach to be ubiquitous. results.content: Building upon the principle of CTL [9] by incorporating domain information into data, our approach is able to identify variables with invariant functional relationships to their direct causes, which we refer to as *common causal mechanisms*, and use the identified common causal mechanisms shared by all domains to further guide the estimation of the remaining causal mechanisms in each individual domain. Built upon existing continuous optimization-based causal discovery methods (see Section II-B), CICME is proposed to recover the causal relationships among variables from multi-domain data, where domains can be defined as any factor of interest that may cause the change of causal mechanisms for certain variables.
